content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The text judges a collision in which the witnesses pressed against the defender's Isaiah 7:14 link are the pressing side's own chain read together (the sign's bounds at 7:16 and 8:3-4 plus the seed-and-loins mechanism verses), which is exactly the situation K-C governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] answered the Isaiah 8:3-4 bound with 8:8 and 9:6-7, while [DR3] presses the sign's own bounds; the sign itself does not state the mechanism.", "rule_words": "the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "Phrase: \"that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.\" Reading one: the closing clause merely reports DR3's chain claim and does no work in the verdict. Reading two: the clause is the judge's own unattributed ground -- the link is UNDERDETERMINED because the sign verse is silent. The clause stands in the judge's voice after the semicolon and the verdict hangs on it, so reading two holds: the judge used the retired test.", "why": "Having recognized the chain-against-chain collision, the judge decided it (as UNDERDETERMINED) on a single verse's silence -- \"the sign itself does not state the mechanism\" -- which is the stating-verse test K-C retires at a judge's seat, while performing no weighing of [CR2]'s chain against [DR3]'s chain by footing."}
